What this gun does
A two-inch, stem-mounted magnetron. The NW100 plate is the chamber interface. The feedthrough and coolant fittings are outside. The target faces into the chamber.
Vacuum joint

The KF25 clamp grips the feedthrough and mating stub. The metal centering ring locates the flanges. Its O-ring seals between their faces. The stub, NW100 plate, and hollow stem form the grounded mount.
Power and insulation

DC or the output of a 13.56 megahertz matching network drives the same center conductor, one at a time. A socket joins the copper tube to the rod. The ceramic guide centers the rod. The ceramic carrier separates the grounded stem from the live head. The external terminal enclosure and carrier retention still need detailing.
The two coolant lines

Each line begins at an external bulkhead. Inside the stem, an angled transition leads to a dielectric section, then a metal tube at the powered head. The dielectric sections interrupt the metal path. The coolant itself can still conduct. Both lines pass through the carrier, locator, and yoke into the copper backplate.
Rear magnet pack

Eight outer magnets surround an annular center magnet. All nine are five millimeters thick in this layout. They sit flush in a separate nonmagnetic locator and touch the rear face of the steel yoke. The copper head seats directly against the front of the yoke. The yoke is at cathode potential.
The copper cooling jacket

The backplate, C-channel core, and target-seat cover are separate copper pieces. Three head screws pass through dry zones around the channel. The divider lies between inlet and outlet so water must sweep around the channel. The closure and tube seals are still open design items.
Follow the water

Blue shows the proposed supply path. Water enters the backplate, travels around the C-shaped channel behind the target, and exits into the orange return. Heat crosses the target seat into the coolant. The moving markers show direction. They do not represent measured flow.
Target and clamp

The 50.8 millimeter aluminum target seats flat against the copper cover. The ring has a 48 millimeter opening and overlaps the target by 1.4 millimeters per side. Three recessed screws, 120 degrees apart, clamp the ring to the seat. Screw threads and preload are not validated.
Shield and target access

The shield bolts to its grounded rear seat. The 72.8 millimeter side bore leaves a two millimeter radial gap around the powered head. The inward lip covers the clamp. The shield comes off toward the chamber interior before the target can be removed. Its 92 millimeter mounting flange must clear the actual chamber port.
Complete assembly and checks

This is the native SolidWorks R06 geometry, with all 45 part instances. The four reported overlaps are at the angled coolant transitions. Before fabrication, resolve those joints, the carrier retention, and the enclosed power termination. Verify seals, cooling, the magnetic field, and electrical clearance in both DC and RF.
